What Is the Next [FTSE 350] Test for BAE Systems plc (LSE:BA.)?
sum: - Компания BAE Systems plc остается заметной в индексах FTSE 350 и FTSE 100, поскольку рынок ищет следующего значимого катализатора.
- Последний шаг необходимо проверить на основе фактических данных, а не рассматривать как окончательный вывод.
- Четкие вехи и последовательное раскрытие информации будут определять следующее прочтение прогноза компании.

Лондонские акции торгуются на неоднозначном фоне, поскольку устойчивые данные по экономическому росту в Великобритании и отдельные корпоративные новости поддерживают часть рынка, в то время как движение цен на драгоценные металлы влияет на активность во всем горнодобывающем секторе. Розничные, финансовые, промышленные и оборонные компании продолжают показывать резко разные результаты по основным показателям, сохраняя в центре сессии поставки конкретных компаний. Внимание вокруг BAE Systems plc (LSE:BA.) переключается на следующий катализатор, ориентированный на конкретную компанию, и доказательства, стоящие за ним. Компания представлена ​​в индексах FTSE 350 и FTSE 100, что делает ее индивидуальный прогресс актуальным как для крупных рынков, так и для дискуссий по эталонным показателям. В рамках промышленных акций внимание сосредоточено на данных о компаниях, а также на направлении более широкого ориентира.

Второе чтение BAE Systems plc начинается с выбора времени. Рынки часто начинают двигаться до того, как операционные изменения становятся полностью заметными, особенно когда положение сектора быстро меняется. Практическая задача состоит в том, чтобы определить, какое раскрытие информации в будущем может подтвердить текущую точку зрения, а какой результат потребует пересмотра ожиданий.

Ее база в сфере промышленных услуг и основных операций дает компании узнаваемую роль, но членство в индексе не может заменить исполнительность. Полезные данные будут получены из поведения клиентов, непрерывности обслуживания, этапов проекта и дисциплинированного использования ресурсов. Эти детали показывают, становится ли стратегия воспроизводимой.

Потенциальная поддержка обеспечивается прозрачностью контрактов, использованием активов и дисциплиной поставок. Эта возможность наиболее эффективна, когда эти качества связаны с четкой последовательностью реализации. Надежный путь помогает рынку понять, что должно произойти дальше, не полагаясь на общие обещания или ажиотаж вокруг одной сессии.

BAE Systems share price rises as free cash flow guidance hiked to £3bn
sum: Profit guidance is unchanged today while upgraded free cash flow guidance appears to reflect customer advance payments rather than any change to trading conditions. However, BAE appears to be trading well and benefiting from structural demand growth in both the UK and US markets. The valuation has eased since our last view in May and I'm happy to stay broadly positive.
BAE Systems' share price has consolidated this year after quadrupling over the last five years. Today's announcement looks solid to me but seems unlikely to prompt any major change to expectations.

- Strong momentum with order intake of £33bn so far this year, and further expected. This compares to a figure of £16.4bn at the end of June, so order intake has increased modestly in H2. Notable orders include c.£1.6bn related to the Global Compat Air Programme and c.£4.3bn of further funding for UK Dreadnought Class nuclear deterrent submarines.
- Free cash flow is now expected to be around £3bn this year, nearly 50% above previous guidance of >£2bn. This is said to reflect the benefit of customer advances received so far.

CEO Charles Woodburn says that strong trading in BAE's Electronic Systems, Air and Platforms & Services sectors offset "subdued growth and margins in our Maritime sector, as we progress through the first-in-class stage of the Type 26 frigate programme."

My reading of this is that completing the first of these new submarine hunter frigates is perhaps taking additional time and resources - hopefully future ships (I believe eight are on order for the Royal Navy) will be quicker.

In the US, BAE singles out munitions as an area of strong demand and says the company is supporting ten of the 12 programmes that are "prioritised for significantly increased production capacity". Space defence is also said to be a key area of focus.

BAE Systems stock in focus after accelerated LRASM sensor deliveries
sum: BAE Systems announced on Tuesday, November 10, that it had delivered all Lot 8 radio-frequency sensors for Lockheed Martin's Long-Range Anti-Ship Missile, or LRASM. The company said the delivery followed an accelerated production schedule and highlighted investments in its electronic warfare facilities. The announcement was published in the BAE Systems newsroom.

BAE Systems supplies the LRASM radio-frequency sensor to Lockheed Martin under a contract running through 2028. The sensor provides guidance technology for a missile designed to engage maritime targets in heavily contested environments, including conditions involving advanced air defenses.

The company said LRASM began as a low-volume production program but is expected to scale significantly in 2026 and beyond. BAE Systems linked the faster delivery schedule to investments in modern electronic warfare facilities that support design, production and testing.

BAE Systems also upgraded the sensor software and completed verification testing. The improvements were delivered digitally without hardware changes, while development of both the software and hardware continues. Engineering, design and manufacturing work is carried out at facilities in Austin, Greenlawn, Nashua and Wayne.

For investors, the update provides another operational signal for BAE Systems' electronic warfare and maritime defense activities. It does not include a new contract value or a change to group guidance, so the immediate financial effect cannot be quantified from the announcement. The longer delivery horizon nevertheless gives the program visibility as defense customers seek higher production capacity.
BAE Systems stock traded at 22.98 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:39 CET on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, 0.09 percent below the Xetra close of Tuesday, November 10.
UK defense shares remain part of the broader FTSE 100 market environment.

My Stocks and Shares ISA has tanked! Here’s what I’m doing
sum: It has been a very difficult spell for my Stocks and Shares ISA recently. Many of my largest holdings have tanked as growth and AI/tech stocks have sold off aggressively. Thursday (5 November) was particularly brutal.
Adding salt to the wounds, even ‘boring’ FTSE 100 stalwarts such as HSBC and BAE Systems have been struggling. Both of these are roughly 20% below their summer highs.
The first thing I need to remember is that volatility and periods of poor performance are par for the course for a long-term investor.
My holding period for a stock is three-to-five years (ideally longer). Therefore, what happens over three-to-five months isn’t that important in the grand scheme of things.
That said, I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t bothered when my portfolio rapidly declines in value. I don’t like it. But I know it’s the price of admission to the stock market.

As always, there’s a Warren Buffett quote that clarifies things: “You’ve got to be prepared, when you buy a stock, to have it go down 50% — or more — and be comfortable with it, as long as you’re comfortable with the holding.”
Another thing I like to do at times like this is to put things into perspective. Returning to HSBC and BAE, for example, these UK shares had a fantastic 2025. So did Rolls-Royce.

Nasdaq slides 1.2% amid renewed pressure on AI stocks
sum: US technology stocks extended their losses on Thursday as Wall Street reacted to the Democrats’ midterm election victories, with investors concerned that increased political scrutiny could slow the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure.
The Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.2% to 25,427.44 at the opening bell, continuing a difficult week for technology shares as investors reassessed the outlook for AI-related investment and regulation.
The broader S&P 500 declined 0.4% to 7,654.89, reflecting weakness among major technology companies that have played an important role in driving US equity market gains.
However, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.5% to 53,595.12, highlighting a divergence between technology stocks and more traditional sectors of the American economy.

Investors appeared to be rotating away from technology shares towards established industrial and other non-technology businesses, amid concerns that Democratic lawmakers could seek greater oversight of AI development and the rapid expansion of data centres.
The election results have brought renewed attention to the electricity consumption, infrastructure requirements and local environmental impact of large-scale AI facilities.

Potential restrictions on new data centre developments could affect expectations for future spending on semiconductors, servers and supporting infrastructure, although the scale and timing of any regulatory changes remain uncertain.

Down 9% in 3 months, could BAE Systems shares be one of the FTSE 100’s best bargains?
sum: BAE Systems' (LSE:BA.) shares are currently (3 November) changing hands for 9% less than they were in the middle of August, and 11% lower than in March, when the stock recorded its 52-week high.
Does this mean the defence contractor's shares are now a bargain?
Savvy investors know that short-term price movements are largely irrelevant. Although it's difficult to ignore monthly fluctuations, it's the long-term trend that matters.

And a look at the graph for BAE Systems shows that its share price has been going in the right direction over the past five years. In fact, since October 2021, it's increased by 275%. This makes it the fourth-best performer on the FTSE 100.

And as the biggest supplier to the Ministry of Defence, I think further growth's likely. On Wednesday (28 October), the UK Chancellor confirmed the government's commitment to meet the NATO target of spending 3% of Gross Domestic Product on defence by 2030, and 3.5% by 2035.
Although no details were provided as to how this was going to be achieved, it stands to reason that BAE Systems will be one of the beneficiaries.

Why? Well, the group's firmly embedded within the UK's military infrastructure — for example, it plays a vital role in supporting the country's nuclear-powered submarines — which means its order book is likely to grow in line with government spending on defence.

The FTSE 100 closed at 10,767.33 points on Monday, 26 October 2026, up 76.97 points or 0.72% from Friday’s close of 10,690.36, according to Reuters and Alliance News closing data. The mid-cap FTSE 250 did even better, rising 1.09% to 24,501.25, its biggest one-day gain since 9 October. The AIM All-Share added 0.9% to 753.18.

The gain came despite a weak session in Asia and recovered part of the ground the index lost last week, when it had closed at 10,752.88 on Wednesday before slipping as oil hit a five-month high. The FTSE 100 remains about 2% below its July record near 10,991.
“The FTSE 100 made a solid start to Budget week as oil prices eased back and despite weak trading across Asia,” said Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell.

Third 6th-Gen Fighter Program Bubbles in Europe as Germany Explores Spain-Sweden Deal
sum: As Germany seeks a new partner to develop its next-generation fighter after the collapse of FCAS, it now faces two choices: join the Global Combat Air Program (GCAP) or forge a new partnership with Sweden and Spain.
If the proposal materializes, Europe could have three sixth-generation fighter programs: GCAP and the French initiative.

In June 2026, the Friedrich Merz administration pulled the plug on the FCAS (Future Combat Air System) that it was pursuing with France and Spain, over irreconcilable differences between industry partners Airbus (representing Germany and Spain) and France’s Dassault Aviation.
Berlin has been seeking a partnership to develop a sixth-generation aircraft ever since.

Earlier this month, reports indicated it held “exploratory talks” about joining the GCAP led by the UK, Japan, and Italy, and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham officially raised Germany’s involvement in GCAP.
However, Airbus had also earlier hinted it could potentially partner with Swedish defense manufacturer Saab to develop its sixth-generation fighter.
German defense officials have reportedly encouraged Berlin to seek a new fighter-aircraft collaboration with Sweden and Spain rather than join an existing deal involving the United Kingdom.

sum: BAE Systems (LSE: BA) shares' 18% drop from their 18 March £23.59 one-year high suggests many investors believe the global security environment is improving. I completely disagree.
The war in Ukraine is ongoing, as is that between the US and Iran, and Iran and Israel. Indeed, the Tehran-backed Houthis have widened the war with attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Even if these conflicts stopped tomorrow, a massive increase in NATO's long-term defence spending has already been agreed. The organisation pledged 5% of GDP to go on defence by 2035. That means a rise of around 64% from today. And as Europe's largest defence firm and the world's sixth-largest, BAE is perfectly positioned to benefit from that.
The 20 main analysts covering BAE have a 12-month price target of £23.23. That represents a 20.4% rise from the £19.29 level at the time of writing.

Bullish sentiment was boosted following BAE's strong H1 2026 results released on 30 July. Management raised full-year guidance across the board for all key measures. For example, underlying earnings before interest and taxes growth was increased from 9%-11% to 10%-12%. It is growth in earnings that is the key driver of share price gains for any stock.
Sales growth guidance jumped from 7%-9% to 8%-10%, and the free cash flow forecast soared 54% to £2bn.

Analysts' confidence in the defence giant achieving these new numbers stems from the strong multi-decade order book. In fact, the H1 numbers saw new orders climb 24% year on year to £16.4bn, with an £84bn order backlog. These figures — and the several massive multi-year deals included within them — provide exceptional earnings visibility for the company.

Down 20%, could BAE Systems shares have more potential than Rolls-Royce?
sum: After a powerful multi-year rally, BAE Systems' (LSE: BA.) shares have experienced a pullback. Currently, they're trading near £19 – around 20% below their all-time highs.
Could they offer more potential than shares in industrial rival Rolls-Royce (LSE: RR.) after this dip? Let's discuss.

BAE Systems' shares are certainly a lot cheaper than Rolls-Royce shares at the moment. Looking at earnings forecasts for 2026, they're currently trading on a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of about 23.
Rolls-Royce shares are sporting a P/E ratio of 34. So they're almost 50% more expensive.

Of course, a P/E ratio in isolation is pretty useless. To get value out of this ratio, we need to look at lots of other factors like revenue and earnings growth, long-term growth potential, and financial strength.

At first glance, the market reaction appears counterintuitive. NATO has effectively confirmed the long-term trend of rising defense spending, while Europe's largest defense contractors continue to enjoy record order backlogs. In theory, Rheinmetall shares should be moving higher.

items.t: Is BAE Systems Expanding Its Presence in the Naval MRO Market?
sum: BAE Systems BAESY continues to strengthen its position in the global naval maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) market through its broad portfolio of ship repair, modernization and sustainment services for military vessels. The company plays an important role in supporting the operational readiness of the U.S. Navy and allied naval forces by providing maintenance, upgrades and lifecycle support for a wide range of naval platforms.

BAE Systems operates one of the largest naval ship repair businesses in the United States, providing maintenance, overhaul, modernization and technical support for amphibious assault ships, destroyers, cruisers and other surface combatants. Its capabilities help extend the service life of naval vessels, improve mission readiness and ensure fleet remain operational in increasingly demanding environments.

Growing geopolitical tensions, rising global defense spending and increasing investments in naval fleet modernization are driving demand for maintenance, repair and overhaul services worldwide. As navies look to extend the operational life of existing vessels while maintaining combat readiness, demand for advanced sustainment and modernization solutions is expected to remain strong.

BAE Systems is well-positioned to benefit from these long-term industry trends through its extensive experience in naval ship repair and modernization, supported by long-standing relationships with the U.S. Navy and allied defense customers. Its strong portfolio of maintenance and sustainment capabilities should enable the company to capitalize on the growing demand for naval MRO services.

BAE Systems Shares Surge as UK’s £15bn Defence Boost Fuels Rally
sum: BAE Systems (LON: BA.) shares surged more than 6% on Thursday, hitting a high of 2,006p before settling around 1,993p as the defence giant extended a powerful two-day rally sparked by the UK government’s long-delayed Defence Investment Plan.

The move has now added well over £3 billion to BAE’s market value since Tuesday’s close, on volume of more than 4 million shares, as investors piled into the stock following confirmation of major new government spending commitments squarely aligned with BAE’s core operations.

Published Tuesday after weeks of delay — a delay that had already cost one Defence Secretary his job — the plan confirms £15 billion in additional funding over four years, taking total planned defence spending to around £300 billion and pushing outlays to 2.7% of GDP by 2029.

Crucially, the money flows directly into BAE’s businesses: £8.6 billion for the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), £63 billion for nuclear deterrent and submarine work, £11 billion for munitions, and £5 billion for drones and autonomous naval systems — covering combat-air, naval, weapons and autonomy divisions alike.
CEO Charles Woodburn told Reuters the funding is “vital to sustaining the specialist skills” underpinning the UK’s defence industrial base.

The rally has been reinforced by bullish broker commentary and appears to have gathered further momentum through Thursday’s session as investors and defence-sector funds continued buying. The gain now vastly outstrips the firepower of BAE’s own £500 million buyback programme launched last month.
Some caution remains: a £4.7 billion funding shortfall in the UK is still unresolved, with defence chiefs having sought £28 billion rather than £15 billion. BAE reports half-year results on July 30.

Here’s Why BAE Systems Was the Biggest FTSE 100 Faller on Monday
sum: BAE Systems (LON: BA.) was the worst performer in the FTSE 100 on Monday, shedding 4.74% to trade around 1,878p — wiping hundreds of millions of pounds off the company’s roughly £55 billion market capitalisation in a single session.

The primary culprit was a change in geopolitical mood. News of a preliminary US–Iran peace deal flooded markets over the weekend, sparking a broad “risk-on” rally in European equities and sending Brent crude tumbling from $87.00 on Friday to $83.18 by Monday afternoon. For a defence stock that had thrived under elevated geopolitical tension, that shift triggered swift and heavy profit-taking.

BAE was not alone. Shell fell 4.35% and BP dropped 3.27% on the same session, both punished by sliding oil prices. But BAE’s decline was the sharpest, reflecting how much of its recent premium was built on geopolitical risk appetite.

Compounding the pressure was ongoing uncertainty surrounding the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) — the next-generation fighter jet project BAE leads alongside Italy’s Leonardo and Japan’s Mitsubishi-backed consortium. The UK government faces a June 30 deadline to approve a £6 billion Defence Investment Plan underpinning the programme, and reports of potential delays have unnerved investors for weeks.
BAE’s valuation also left it exposed. At roughly 28 times earnings, the stock offers little buffer when the macro wind shifts direction.
The company’s fundamentals remain strong — a record £83.6 billion order backlog and full-year guidance intact — but for now, the market is not in the mood to pay a premium for defence.

items.t: The companies making billions from the Iran war
sum: As households across the globe count the costs of the US-Israel war in Iran, some companies have been counting bumper profits instead.
The uncertainty sparked by the conflict, and Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, is driving up the cost of living and hitting the budgets of firms, families and governments.
But while some have been pushed to the brink, others, whose core businesses are more profitable in a war or who benefit from volatile energy prices, have seen record earnings.
Here are some of the sectors and companies making billions while the Middle East conflict continues.

The biggest economic impact of the war so far has been a surge in energy prices. Around a fifth of the world's oil and gas is transported through the Strait of Hormuz, but those shipments effectively ground to a halt at the end of February.
The result has been a rollercoaster of price movements on energy markets, with some of the world's biggest oil and gas companies benefiting.
The main beneficiaries have been European oil giants, who have trading arms so have been able to gain from sharp price movements boosting profits.

items.t: Mounting geopolitical tensions have changed the game for BAE Systems
sum: Rising geopolitical tensions and expanding UK and European defence budgets following the Russia’s invasion of Ukraine have created a substantial tailwind for BAE Systems, with the shares delivering nearly 400% in total shareholder returns over the last five years data.

The shares have comfortably outperformed the FTSE 100 and the global defence sector. Before the invasion of Ukraine BAE shares traded on forecast PE (price to earnings) ratio of 12 times, less than half its current rating.
This implies that structural industry drivers have been increasingly recognised by the stock market.
After the invasion of Ukraine global military spending increased almost 7% in 2023 to reach a record $2.44 trillion, followed by a further 11% increase to $2.72 trillion in 2024.

Adjusted for inflation the increase in 2024 was the largest annual increase since the Cold War. After struggling to meet the 2% of GDP target for years, NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) members have upped their game.

In Europe spending increased by 17% in 2024 and Germany’s budget leapt to $107 billion. A NATO summit in June 2025 saw allies commit to spending a minimum 3.5% of GDP on core military requirements by 2035.

An additional 1.5% of GDP is expected to be allocated to adjacent spending on cyber defence to protect critical infrastructure. In total, the new ‘gold standard’ for the NATO alliance could reach 5% of GDP over the next decade.

Foreign Policy Journal reported that first-half sales grew 9 percent and underlying EBIT increased 11 percent from the prior-year period. The comparison shifts attention from contract headlines to backlog conversion, cash generation and delivery across long-cycle defense programs.

Best Defence Stocks to Watch in 2026
sum: Global rearmament is reshaping investment portfolios. With NATO spending accelerating, stockpiles being replenished and multi-decade contracts being locked in, defence stocks have moved from niche holding to mainstream consideration.

Defence stocks are now arguably benefiting from a structural multi-year spending cycle due to increasing geopolitical risk. The largest companies in the sector enjoy large order backlogs, long-term government contracts and exposure to both US and European rearmament programmes, which may be worth some consideration.
The macro environment for defence stocks in 2026 is arguably the strongest it’s been in a generation.
Conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East have depleted Western military stockpiles, forcing urgent replenishment programmes that are directly benefitting the largest contractors.
Simultaneously, NATO members are committing record shares of GDP to defence budgets, with several European nations pushing well beyond the 2% target that was once considered aspirational.

European rearmament is perhaps the standout story. Germany has reversed decades of spending restraint, Poland is dramatically scaling up procurement, and the broader continent is now funding programmes in ammunition, air defence, armoured vehicles and naval assets that will run well into the 2030s. That structural shift has propelled European defence names to multi-year highs.
On the US side, the recently rechristened Department of War continues to see its budget rise, with global defence spending projected to approach three trillion dollars by the end of the decade.

Germany's Hensoldt and Britain's BAE Systems were among the top performers in the Stoxx 600, up close to 5% and around 6%, respectively. Defense name Renk rose more than 3%, and Leonardo gained more than 2%, paring earlier gains. The broader Stoxx 600 index fell more than 1%, touching a two-week low.
Stateside, U.S. firms Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman rose more than 3% and about 6%, respectively. The S&P 500 traded just above the flatline, rebounding from earlier losses.

With South Korean markets closed Monday, regional activity in Asia-Pacific defense sector was somewhat muted. Japan's defense heavyweights Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and IHI rose roughly 3% each, while Singapore's ST Engineering climbed 2.8%.

The moves come after the U.S. and Israel launched widespread attacks on Iran over the weekend that killed Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, ending his 36-year rule. Retaliatory strikes by Iran against U.S. bases in the Middle East killed three U.S. service members.
Prospects of an escalation also led oil prices and energy companies' shares to surge.

BAE Systems Signals Steady Earnings Growth After Record Year
UK's BAE Systems forecasts years of growth in ‘new era’ of defence spending, backlog hits record
Britain’s BAE Systems sets sights on defense spending boom amid record order backlog
sum: BAE Systems attracted record orders in 2025, and now the UK defense staple is setting its sights on years of growth amid a global ramp-up in spending.
Its shares rose 3.6% on Wednesday after its full-year earnings report showed sales soared 10% last year to reach a record £30.7 billion ($41.7 billion).
That helped push operating profits to £2.93 billion, a 9% year-on-year increase, as revenues grew 8% to £28.3 billion.
The FTSE 100-listed company, which manufactures a range of aircraft, weapons, munitions and warships, saw its order backlog hit £83.6 billion, a £5.8 billion increase from 2024.

Now, BAE is preparing to capitalize on years of future growth as geopolitical fissures usher in what CEO Charles Woodburn called a "new era of defense spending" driven by "escalating security challenges."
The company expects sales to grow by between 7% and 9% in 2026, with guidance for cumulative free cash flow between 2026 and 2028 in excess of £6 billion.

"We're well positioned to provide both the advanced conventional systems and disruptive technologies needed to protect the nations we serve now and into the future," Woodburn said in a statement accompanying Wednesday's earnings.

BAE Systems Earnings Preview: Can Full-Year Results Extend the Share Price Rally?
sum: BAE Systems (LON: BA.) will report full-year 2025 earnings on Wednesday, with analysts expecting another year of strong growth underpinned by elevated global defence spending and solid order momentum.
Market expectations point to performance in line with the group’s November guidance, which called for “good growth” in sales and underlying EBIT, alongside robust cash generation.
Company-compiled consensus forecasts FY25 sales of £30.6 billion, with estimates ranging from £30.5 billion to £30.8 billion.

Underlying EBIT is projected at £3.29 billion, while underlying earnings per share are expected to reach 74.2 pence. Free cash flow is forecast at £1.53 billion, comfortably above the group’s guidance of more than £1.1 billion.
Analysts see this momentum extending into 2026, with consensus pointing to further increases in sales, profits and dividends.

In its last trading update, the company reaffirmed that it was on track to deliver mid- to high-single-digit growth across all key metrics, supported by sustained demand, a sizeable order backlog and its multinational programme footprint.
Currency movements also remain a factor, given the group’s exposure to U.S. dollar-denominated revenue.

sum: Saab AB is a Sweden-based defence and aerospace company listed in Stockholm, with its class B shares closely followed in the context of order intake, programme delivery and wider defence-sector developments. Explore SAAB’s recent price action, third-party price targets and technical analysis.

Saab (SAAB_B) is trading around 691.5 Swedish Krona (SEK) during intraday trade on 15 January 2026, within a session range of 679.7 SEK–698.6 SEK as of 1:29pm UTC. Past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results.

Price action is developing amid a series of defence-related headlines for Saab, including a 1.5bn SEK order from Sweden’s Defence Materiel Administration for the Trackfire Remote Weapon Station, booked in the fourth quarter of 2025 (Saab, 9 January 2026), and the 14 January 2026 launch of Poland’s second signals intelligence vessel, ORP Henryk Zygalski, under the Delfin programme (Saab, 14 January 2026). These contracts add to an already elevated order backlog, after Saab disclosed roughly 138bn SEK of 2025 order intake, with analysts noting that investor focus in 2026 has shifted towards the company’s capacity to execute and deliver long-cycle programmes such as Gripen fighters and A26 submarines (Inderes, 29 December 2025).

As of 15 January 2026, third-party Saab stock predictions indicate a wide dispersion of 12-month views into 2026, reflecting differing assumptions around defence spending, programme execution and valuation multiples. These targets are typically framed as 12-month fair-value estimates, rather than specific year-end prices, and can change as new orders, results and guidance are released.

Kepler Cheuvreux raised its SAAB_B stock forecast to 420.00 SEK, while maintaining a Reduce rating, framing the figure as a 12-month price objective. The broker cited strong order intake and a potentially high book-to-bill ratio for 2025, while flagging margin pressure, higher central costs and elevated valuation multiples as of that date (Investing.com, 6 January 2026).
Fintel’s snapshot of SAAB_B stock forecasts shows an average one-year target of 483.56 SEK, within a published range of 272.70 SEK–745.50 SEK.

items.t: BAE Systems Leads FTSE 100 as Defence Stocks Extend Rally on Geopolitical Tensions
sum: BAE Systems led gains on the FTSE 100 in early trading, emerging as the index’s strongest performer after U.S. President Donald Trump vowed to significantly increase military spending.

Shares in Britain’s largest defence company climbed as much as 6.9%, supported by expectations of higher U.S. defence budgets. BAE Systems generates nearly half of its revenues in the United States, making it particularly sensitive to shifts in American military spending policy.

The rally extended across the wider defence sector, lifting stocks on both of the UK’s main equity indices. On the FTSE 250, Chemring led gains, rising as much as 4.2%. The company supplies countermeasures used on Typhoon and F-35 fighter jets, leaving it well positioned to benefit from increased defence procurement.

Overall, defence companies across the FTSE 100 and FTSE 250 rose by around 3.3%, putting the sector on course for a fifth consecutive day of gains and reinforcing its status as one of the strongest-performing areas of the UK stock market.

Investor appetite for defence shares has been underpinned by escalating geopolitical tensions and signs of growing fractures in the global political order. Markets have been unsettled following reports that U.S. forces captured Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, alongside President Trump’s renewed threats to take control of Greenland.

Further adding to global uncertainty, the United States has seized two Venezuela-linked oil tankers in the Atlantic Ocean, raising concerns about energy supply disruption and the risk of wider international confrontation.

Periods of heightened geopolitical risk have historically supported defence stocks, as governments prioritise military readiness and national security. The latest developments have reinforced expectations of sustained defence spending growth, helping UK defence companies outperform the broader market.
